newsitem.title: USA: Campaigns pick PBS' Jim Lehrer to moderate debates.
newsitem.headline: Campaigns pick PBS' Jim Lehrer to moderate debates.

text.p: The campaigns of President Clinton and Republican Bob Dole have recommended PBS-TV's Jim Lehrer as sole moderator for the presidential and vice presidential debates, a spokesman for Lehrer said Sunday.
Cory Shields, communications director for PBS-TV's "NewsHour with Jim Lehrer," said no final decision on the debates' moderator had been made yet by the bipartisan Commission on Presidential Debates.
But he said Lehrer would be honoured to moderate the debates if that was the commission's wish.

"The Dole and Clinton campaigns have recommended that Jim Lehrer be the sole moderator for all the presidential and vice presidential debates," Shields said. "Jim has said, if asked, it would be an honour and a privelege."
Lehrer moderated a debate between Democratic and Republican congressional leaders in Williamsburg, Va. Sunday. He also helped moderate the presidential debates in 1988 and 1992.
Negotiators for the two campaigns Saturday settled a squabble over the timing and format of the presidential debates, the first of which is scheduled for Oct. 6 in Hartford, Connecticut.

A second debate between Clinton and Dole is planned as a town hall meeting for Oct. 16 in San Diego, with Vice President Al Gore and Dole's running mate, Jack Kemp, to debate Oct. 9 in St. Petersburg, Florida.
